evidence.positive: Against the running app (localhost:58842, mayo-mayo tenant) I created patient or2804-fake-507e1dfe / case 63131 with procedure p-cesarean-delivery, the only bundled procedure whose pathways are acuity-scoped (DB confirms two rows in mayo-mayo.antibiotic_pathways with antibiotic_pathway_acuities of ELECTIVE and EMERGENT|URGENT). Setting acuity ELECTIVE (PATCH /api/admin/patients/{pmrn}/operations/{caseId}/acuity) then reading GET .../antibiotic-candidates returned outcome RECOMMENDED, caseAcuity ELECTIVE, recommended = [CEFAZOLIN] only, with pathway pos=0 acuities=["ELECTIVE"] appliesToCase=true and pathway pos=1 acuities=["EMERGENT","URGENT"] appliesToCase=false. Flipping the same case to URGENT returned recommended = [CEFAZOLIN, AZITHROMYCIN] with the appliesToCase flags exactly inverted; EMERGENT matched the same multi-value cell. A separate unscoped case (p-mastectomy, acuity null) still resolved RECOMMENDED with acuities=[] appliesToCase=true, so blank-acuity pathways were not narrowed. Cache-drop half: with acuity ELECTIVE I warmed the real cache by firing POST /api/admin/events/category-event INDUCTION_START and confirmed Valkey key 'antibiotic-resolution-v3/tenant:mayo-mayo/op:01a0582e-2889-7f3d-9440-20046f5edce5' held the CEFAZOLIN-only protocol; injecting a Mayo SIU^S14 (POST /api/admin/hl7-inbound-messages/send) with PV1-4=Urg and no AIS segments moved operations.acuity to URGENT and the Valkey EXISTS went 1 -> 0, and re-warming produced [[CEFAZOLIN, AZITHROMYCIN],[CLINDAMYCIN, GENTAMICIN, AZITHROMYCIN]]. Import check: the boot log carries 'p-cesarean-delivery has no pathway for NON_URGENT, no acuity, so such a case resolves to no guidance', which is exactly the runtime gap.
evidence.negative: The inverse cases do not happen. (1) A case carrying no acuity matches only pathways naming none: on the same cesarean case with acuity null the debug read returned outcome NOT_CONFIGURED, caseAcuity null and appliesToCase=false on BOTH pathways, i.e. the elective and the urgent regimens were both withheld rather than one being guessed; the app log shows 'matched no antibiotic pathway for p-cesarean-delivery: 2 configured, procedure risk LOW case acuity none'. (2) NON_URGENT, a value no bundled guideline names, also resolved NOT_CONFIGURED with both pathways appliesToCase=false and the matching log line '... case acuity NON_URGENT' - agreeing with the import-time warning, which is the shared-predicate claim. (3) Cache drop does not fire when acuity is unchanged: injecting the same SIU with PV1-4=Elec against the already-ELECTIVE case persisted the case (log 'Persisted HL7-sourced Operation id=01a0582e-2889-7f3d-9440-20046f5edce5') yet Valkey EXISTS stayed 1, so the drop is conditional on the acuity actually changing rather than firing on every scheduling message.
evidence.red_check: Ran the pre-fix predicate in the container. Recompiled orci/src/main/java/.../ProcedureAntibioticCandidateService.java with configuredPathways' filter reverted to the pre-PR risk-only form (pathway.getRisk() == null || pathway.getRisk() == risk) plus a distinctive WARN, compiled against the container's own /app/libs + /app/classes with lombok on the processor path, backed up all five shipped class files (md5 of the main class c305117c8e0c6336f2041a92c9bf84fd), copied the patched classes into /app/classes (md5 9cd91532fa8adf0b95244019e6ef352d) and restarted. The app booted and the ELECTIVE cesarean case then went RED: recommended became [CEFAZOLIN] AND [CEFAZOLIN, AZITHROMYCIN] - the elective case being offered the regimen written for the urgent one, which is the exact defect the ticket names - and the null-acuity case went from NOT_CONFIGURED to RECOMMENDED with both regimens. Log line while red: 'OR2804_PREFIX_RISK_ONLY_FILTER applied for p-cesarean-delivery: acuity ELECTIVE ignored, 2 of 2 pathways kept'. I then restored the five backed-up class files (md5 of the main class back to c305117c8e0c6336f2041a92c9bf84fd), restarted, and re-ran the positive case: ELECTIVE again returns CEFAZOLIN only, and the signature appears nowhere in the log after the restore restart. A class swap of AntibioticPathway itself was deliberately not attempted because orci-models is Hibernate bytecode-enhanced at build time, so a recompiled entity class would not have been a faithful substitute.

red_check_signature: OR2804_PREFIX_RISK_ONLY_FILTER applied for p-cesarean-delivery: acuity ELECTIVE ignored
caveats: The ticket says acuity is read through CaseClassification; on the build under test it is read through CaseAcuity via Operation.getAcuity(), the rename that landed with the follow-on tickets. Same vocabulary, same behaviour, but the ticket text and the code no longer use the same name.
Only p-cesarean-delivery is acuity-scoped in any bundled tenant file, and only in mayo; demo and mgb have no acuity-scoped rows, so the whole scoping surface was exercised through that one procedure.

The import warning was observed only for an acuity gap. The risk-and-acuity crossed gap and the risk-only gap exist in unit tests but no bundled file produces one at boot, so I did not see those two variants fire at runtime.

The debugger's React tab (AntibioticCandidatesTab.tsx, which now shows acuity beside risk) was not rendered in a browser. I exercised the API that feeds it and confirmed acuities and appliesToCase are in the payload; the UI change is an adjunct on main rather than one of the ticket's five deliverables.
The cache-drop path was driven through the Mayo SIU processor, the only caller of HL7ProcessingContext.saveOperation, so no other feed was covered.
The acuity-changing SIU carried no AIS segments to isolate acuity as the trigger; a real Epic SIU carries procedures, which forces the drop regardless of acuity.

automation.assessment: Backend unit coverage of the scoping itself is already strong and does not need duplicating: AntibioticPathwayResolutionSpecTest has 73 tests including acuityScopedPathwayAppliesOnlyAtThatAcuity, acuityCellNamingSeveralValuesMatchesAnyOfThem, unscopedPathwayAppliesAtEveryAcuity, caseWithoutAcuityMatchesOnlyUnscopedPathways, caseWithoutAcuityAgainstFullyScopedProcedure_isNotConfigured, nonUrgentCaseAgainstAConfigThatDoesNotNameIt_isNotConfigured, acuityAndRiskAreBothRequired and acuityIsSharedAcrossTheProceduresOfOneCase; AntibioticPathwayCSVImporterTest has 45 including the four uncovered-scope reporting tests and bundledMayoFileScopesCesareanDeliveryByAcuity. The real gap is the fifth deliverable: nothing asserts that a scheduling message which changes acuity drops the cached resolution. MayoHL7SiuCaseSchedulingProcessorTest asserts the persisted acuity but never touches RedisService, and ProcedureAntibioticCandidateCacheTest covers the cache in isolation without the HL7 writer. The conditional nature of the drop is the part most likely to rot silently, since a refactor that made it unconditional would still pass every current test.
proposed_tests: MayoHL7SiuCaseSchedulingProcessorTest: an SIU whose PV1-4 changes an existing case's acuity verifies redisService.deleteValue with ProcedureAntibioticCandidateService.SCOPE and the case's cache key, and asserts the delete happens after commit rather than before.

MayoHL7SiuCaseSchedulingProcessorTest: an SIU repeating the acuity already stored, with no AIS segments, asserts redisService.deleteValue is never called for the antibiotic scope - the negative that the current suite cannot fail on.
MayoHL7SiuCaseSchedulingProcessorTest: an SIU with an unmapped PV1-4 leaves the stored acuity untouched and drops nothing, so a junk admission type cannot silently widen a scoped case.

AntibioticPathwayResolutionSpecTest: assert the 'matched no antibiotic pathway' diagnostic is emitted for a fully acuity-scoped procedure on an acuity-less case, since that log line is the only signal a configuration gap is silencing alerts.

jira_comment:
Verdict: deploy-ready.

Positive: An elective cesarean on the Mayo tenant resolved to cefazolin alone while the urgent/emergent pathway was marked not applicable, and the same case flipped to urgent resolved to cefazolin plus azithromycin.
Negative: The same case with no acuity, and with non-urgent acuity, matched neither pathway and resolved to no guidance, matching the uncovered-scope warning the import already logged at boot.
Red check: Swapping the pre-fix risk-only pathway filter into the running container made the elective case offer the urgent regimen as well; the shipped class was restored and the elective case returned to cefazolin alone.

Automation: Pathway scoping and import warnings are already well covered by unit tests; the untested part is the cache drop on a scheduling message that changes acuity, which is proposed as new coverage.
